translationRepairs: He was soon summoned to the Grand Council to conduct state business.
He was soon summoned into the Grand Secretariat to conduct state business.
入閣治事 is cabinet service in the Grand Secretariat (內閣), not the Grand Council (軍機處); the proposed replacement restores that office.
He was soon assigned again to assist the chief tutor of the Upper Study.
He was soon assigned again to serve as chief tutor of the Upper Study.
在上書房總師傅上行走 places San Bao in the chief-tutor post itself; “assist … under a chief tutor” invents a superior he did not serve.
Soon afterward he was again ordered to serve on duty under the chief tutor of the Upper Study.
Soon afterward he was again ordered to serve on duty as chief tutor of the Upper Study.
The same 在…總師傅上行走 idiom means duty as chief tutor, not service under one; “under” reverses rank.
Yong Gui impeached him and asked to retire.
Yong Gui impeached him and requested that he be retired.
請休致 continues 論劾 of the incompetent prefect; s0052 then records Hongquan’s dismissal, so the retirement request is not Yong Gui’s own.
Governor-General Ka'erjishan impeached again; the emperor stripped Hongquan of office on his behalf.
Governor-General Ka'erjishan impeached again; the emperor thereupon stripped Hongquan of office.
上為奪洪銓職 marks the emperor acting on the renewed impeachment, not a dismissal granted as a favor “on his behalf.”
Garrison colonies were opened at Urumqi, Kuche, Toksan, Karashahr, Changji, and Luokelun, yielding over thirty-five thousand eight hundred piculs in the autumn harvest.
Garrison colonies were opened at Urumqi, Piqan (Pichan), Toksan, Karashahr, Changji, and Luokelun, yielding over thirty-five thousand eight hundred piculs in the autumn harvest.
闢展 is Piqan/Pichan; 庫車 (Kuche) appears only in the following unit, so the original conflates two places.
At Urumqi, Kuche, Toksan, Karashahr, Changji, and Luokelun garrison farms were all established; the autumn harvest yielded more than thirty-five thousand eight hundred piculs of grain.
At Urumqi, Piqan (Pichan), Toksan, Karashahr, Changji, and Luokelun garrison farms were all established; the autumn harvest yielded more than thirty-five thousand eight hundred piculs of grain.
The literal field repeats the same 闢展→Kuche misidentification; Piqan (Pichan) is the correct place-name.

He memorialized for canal dredging and expanded farming, proposing a canal of over forty li southeast from the Hesele River to irrigate Hesele Buyi; where the swift Cai Tuoyong River ran steep, he urged higher dikes, stone cutting, and measures to reduce the current.

He memorialized for canal dredging and expanded farming, proposing a canal of over forty li southeast from the Hesele River to irrigate Hesele Buyi; where the swift Caituoyong River ran steep, he urged higher dikes, stone cutting, and measures to reduce the current.
材托庸河 is a hydronym, not a river named with the surname Cai; dropping 材 still omits a syllable of the received name, so render it as one word, Caituoyong.

He memorialized requesting dredging of canals and promotion of agriculture, proposing to dredge a canal of more than forty li southeast from the Hesele River to draw water into Hesele Buyi; the Cai Tuoyong River ran swift and steep, where dikes and dams should be increased, mountain stone cut, and the water's force weakened.

He memorialized requesting dredging of canals and promotion of agriculture, proposing to dredge a canal of more than forty li southeast from the Hesele River to draw water into Hesele Buyi; the Caituoyong River ran swift and steep, where dikes and dams should be increased, mountain stone cut, and the water's force weakened.
The original splits 材 as the surname Cai; the proposed “Tuoyong River” deletes 材. Keep the full hydronym as Caituoyong.
When the emperor returned, Jingyi had an audience; finding him weak after illness, the emperor told him to rest and not force himself to walk.
When the emperor returned, Jingyi had an audience; finding him weak after illness, the emperor told him to rest and not force himself to attend duty.
勿勉強行走 after 病後衰弱 is an order not to force court attendance, not a warning against physical walking.
He was soon appointed to the Huizhou-Chaozhou-Jieyang Circuit and then acted as grain and courier intendant.
He was soon appointed to the Huizhou-Jiaying-Chaozhou Circuit and then acted as grain and courier intendant.
惠嘉潮道 is the Huizhou–Jiaying–Chaozhou circuit; 嘉 is Jiaying (嘉應), not Jieyang (揭陽).
Shortly afterward he was appointed to the Huizhou-Chaozhou-Jieyang Circuit and then transferred to act as grain and courier intendant.
Shortly afterward he was appointed to the Huizhou-Jiaying-Chaozhou Circuit and then transferred to act as grain and courier intendant.
The literal field has the same 嘉→Jieyang error; Jiaying is required by 惠嘉潮道.
When the emperor returned to the capital and Jingyi had an audience, because Jingyi was weak after illness he was ordered to rest and recuperate in peace and not force himself to walk.
When the emperor returned to the capital and Jingyi had an audience, because Jingyi was weak after illness he was ordered to rest and recuperate in peace and not force himself to attend duty.
The literal likewise takes 行走 as walking; the command is not to force attendance on duty.

When the river breached, Governor-General Fang Guancheng impeached Ying Lian for silt-choked ditches and inset revetments that had burst and collapsed an upstream dike above water level; Ying Lian had kept silent about it, delaying essential repairs.

When the river breached, Governor-General Fang Guancheng impeached Ying Lian for silt-choked ditches and inset revetments that had burst and collapsed a moon-shaped dike above the water; Ying Lian had kept silent about it, delaying essential repairs.
月堤 is a moon-shaped (crescent) dike; “upstream dike” is invented and drops the technical term.

The river breached; Governor-General Fang Guancheng impeached Ying Lian, charging that silted ditches and inset revetments had burst and breached the upper-stage dike above the water line; he concealed this without reporting it, thereby delaying urgent repair work.

The river breached; Governor-General Fang Guancheng impeached Ying Lian, charging that silted ditches and inset revetments had burst and collapsed the above-water moon-shaped dike; he concealed this without reporting it, thereby delaying urgent repair work.
水上月堤 is an above-water moon-shaped dike, not an “upper-stage dike.”
He rose to commander of the Bordered Yellow Banner guard corps in the Imperial Household Department.
He rose to commander of the Plain Yellow Banner guard corps in the Imperial Household Department.
正黃旗 is the Plain Yellow Banner; 鑲黃旗 would be Bordered Yellow, which the Chinese does not say.
Through repeated promotions he became commander of the guards of the Bordered Yellow Banner in the Imperial Household Department.
Through repeated promotions he became commander of the guards of the Plain Yellow Banner in the Imperial Household Department.
The literal repeats 正黃旗 as Bordered Yellow; Plain Yellow is the banner named in the office title.
He became Minister of Punishments while retaining his posts as Vice Minister of Revenue and Manchu commander of the Bordered Yellow Banner.
He became Minister of Punishments while retaining his posts as Vice Minister of Revenue and Manchu commander of the Plain Yellow Banner.
正黃旗滿洲都統 is Manchu commander-in-chief of the Plain Yellow Banner, not the Bordered Yellow.
He was transferred to Minister of Punishments, still concurrently holding the posts of Vice Minister of Revenue and commander-in-chief of the Manchu Bordered Yellow Banner.
He was transferred to Minister of Punishments, still concurrently holding the posts of Vice Minister of Revenue and commander-in-chief of the Manchu Plain Yellow Banner.
The literal has the same banner error; 正黃旗 is Plain Yellow.
For the Qianlong Emperor's sixtieth birthday he wrote a hymn modeled on the Sacred Edict preface and presented it to the throne; the Emperor was pleased.
For the Qianlong Emperor's sixtieth birthday he wrote a hymn modeled on the Preface to the Sacred Teachings and presented it to the throne; the Emperor was pleased.
聖教序 is the Preface to the Sacred Teachings, not the Sacred Edict (聖諭).
Ji Yun. Ji Yun, style Xiaolan, was a native of Xian County in Zhili.
Ji Yun, style Xiaolan, was a native of Xian County in Zhili.
The leading 紀昀 is the biography heading fused into the unit, not a second sentence; doubling “Ji Yun.” is an artifact of that fusion.
When the former Liangjiang salt transport commissioner Lu Jianceng fell from favor, Yun—his kinsman by marriage—was stripped of office for leaking word, exiled to Urumqi, and later released.
When the former Lianghuai salt transport commissioner Lu Jianceng fell from favor, Yun—his kinsman by marriage—was stripped of office for leaking word, exiled to Urumqi, and later released.
兩淮 names the Lianghuai salt administration, not Liangjiang (兩江).

The former Liangjiang salt transport commissioner Lu Jianceng had fallen afoul of the throne; Yun was related by marriage and was dismissed for leaking information, exiled to Urumqi, then released and returned.

The former Lianghuai salt transport commissioner Lu Jianceng had fallen afoul of the throne; Yun was related by marriage and was dismissed for leaking information, exiled to Urumqi, then released and returned.
The literal repeats 兩淮 as Liangjiang; Lianghuai is required.
Chastising the late-Ming habit of public lecturing, and with the books of the Five Song Masters being what the examination system prized, he dared not openly declare agreement or disagreement;

Taking warning from the late-Ming habit of public lecturing, and with the books of the Five Song Masters being what the examination system prized, he dared not openly declare agreement or disagreement;
懲明季講學之習 means taking warning from late-Ming lecturing, not chastising or punishing that habit.
He was then sent to Mukden to collate the Wenshu Pavilion collection and died there.
He was then sent to Mukden to collate the Wensu Pavilion collection and died there.
文溯閣 is the Wensu Pavilion; Wenshu would be 文殊, a different name.
He was further ordered to go to Mukden to collate the books stored in the Wenshu Pavilion, and died in Mukden.
He was further ordered to go to Mukden to collate the books stored in the Wensu Pavilion, and died in Mukden.
The literal likewise misreads 文溯閣 as Wenshu; Wensu is the pavilion in Mukden.
